description: Two independent 32-step recorders, each capturing a CV and a gate on every clock and looping them back, polyphonic to sixteen channels

params.text: Records the CV and gate inputs of that side for one full loop length, then stops on its own
Records the CV and gate inputs of that side over the existing loop for as long as it is held down
Erases the CV and gate of all 32 steps of that side, on every polyphonic channel, the moment it is pressed rather than on a clock
Sets the loop length of that side in steps, a reading of 0 giving one step and 31 the longest the knob reaches
Moves the play and record position of that side through the 32-step buffer, 0 to 31 steps

inputs.text: Advances both recorders by one step on a rising edge; recording and the outputs move only on this edge
A rising edge sets both recorders back to their first step
A rising edge records the CV and gate inputs of that side for one full loop length, then stops on its own
Records the CV and gate inputs of that side over the existing loop while this gate is high, reading high at 1V and low again at 0.5V
A rising edge erases the CV and gate of all 32 steps of that side, on every polyphonic channel
Moves the play and record position of that side on by one step per volt, added to the shift knob
Lengthens the loop of that side by one step per volt, added to the length knob, with 32 steps the limit
The CV recorded into that side; its channel count, or the gate input's, sets how many polyphonic channels are recorded and played back
The gate recorded into that side, stored as whatever voltage is present when the clock arrives

outputs.text: The recorded CV of that side at the current step, renewed on each clock
The recorded gate of that side at the current step, renewed on each clock

notes: Both recorders move only on a rising edge at the clock input, so with nothing patched there the outputs never change, and nothing is recorded however the record buttons are used
A side plays back as many polyphonic channels as are patched to its cv and gate inputs at that moment, so unpatching them leaves its outputs carrying nothing
